newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity extends gain on cash, outages.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity extends gain on cash, outages.

text.p: A price spike in the spot western power market Tuesday and reports of scattered plant outages lifted the NYMEX electricity complex out of its recent trading range.
"The cash came out strong. The floor took it up," said one Houston power trader.

April California-Oregon Border (COB) futures settled at their highest since January 23, up 69 cents at $10.60 a megawatt hour (MWh). May COB finished up 40 cents at $10.60. Other COB contracts ended flat to 45 cents higher.

April Palo Verde (PV) futures settled up 84 cents at $15.24, posting its highest level since Christmas. May PV finished up 32 cents at $14.82. Most other active PV months ended flat to 10 cents higher.
A 750 megawatt (MW) unit at the Four Corners coal-fired power plant in New Mexico was shut this morning for repairs, and expected to return to service Thursday.
A 350 MW San Juan coal-fired unit also in New Mexico was shut Sunday, but its restart is unknown at this time.
Moreover, restart of the 1,070 MW San Onofre nuclear unit 2 in San Clemente, Calif., was planned for March 20.
Arizona Public's 1,221 MW Palo Verde nuclear unit 3 was expected to return to service from a scheduled maintenance and refueling shutdown in early April.

In additional to those outages, some hydroelectric projects in the Northwest scaled back production, where water flows is being held in preparation for fish migration next month or snowpack figures fell last month.
Firm, peak bulk power scheduled for Wednesday at COB rose $3.00-3.50/MWh to $17.00-18.50, while deliveries with same terms at PV jumped $2.00-3.00 to $20.00-22.00.
Cool, wet conditions are expected to settle over the Northwest region over the next five days with temperatures averaging four to eight degrees Fahrenheit below normal through to the end of the week.
Most of the Southwest would enjoy dry and much above normal temperatures through Friday.
Most brokers and traders said the complex's rise will likely continue Wednesday.
"I think it's going to continue going up. There's some strength behind it," said one Houston futures trader.
A few dealers warned the rally in power futures could ehd readily once the underlying cash prices begin to ease.
